issues.legal_issue: A slump sale of a land-development business as a going concern does not produce taxable profit from stock-in-trade when no part of the slump price is attributable to that stock.
material_facts: The business bought land, developed it, and then sold it; its development activities included opening roads, laying drains and sanitary arrangements, providing electricity, and providing for a school.
The business was transferred as a whole to a company as a going concern for a lump-sum consideration, paid in shares.
The agreement’s schedule stated a value for the land, but the court found that this reflected its cost in the vendors’ books, not an evaluation of its value on the transfer date.
There was no evidence that the land had been evaluated on the transfer date, and no part of the slump price was attributable to the cost of the land.
issues.conclusion: The sale was of the whole concern, and no part of the slump price was attributable to the cost of the land. No part of the slump price was taxable; the referred question was answered in the negative and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Income-tax Act, 1922, the sale of a whole concern as a going concern does not by itself give rise to taxable income. The relevant inquiry is whether a portion of the slump price is attributable to stock-in-trade. The court applied Commissioner of Income-tax, Kerala v. West Coast Chemicals and Industries Ltd. (46 I.T.R. 135) and Doughty v. Commissioner of Taxes ([1927] A.C. 327). A business of buying, developing, and selling land is distinguishable from one purely buying and selling land, and a scheduled land value alone does not establish that part of the slump price is attributable to land sold.

rule.if: going_concern_slump_sale and land_development_business and no_current_land_valuation_evidence and no_slump_price_attributable_to_stock

predicates.going_concern_slump_sale: The business was transferred as a whole for a lump-sum price as a going concern.
predicates.land_development_business: The business bought land, developed it, and then sold it.
predicates.no_current_land_valuation_evidence: No evidence showed that the land was evaluated at its value on the transfer date.
predicates.no_slump_price_attributable_to_stock: No part of the lump-sum price was attributable to the cost of the land held as stock-in-trade.

issues.definition: When a whole land-development business is transferred as a going concern, there is no taxable part of the lump-sum price if there is no evidence of a current land valuation and no part of the price is attributable to stock-in-trade.
